label: Divine lordship grounded in creaturely subjection
term: divine lordship as a relative appellation in ST I q.13 a.7
definition: God is really called Lord insofar as the creature is really subject to him. The subjection is real in the creature, and the converse relation in God is a relation of reason. Predication follows the creature’s relation and can apply temporally without an intrinsic change in God.
